# Lunar Landing Site Navigator – Project Summary

## 1. Challenge Overview

The Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge focuses on finding and evaluating suitable landing locations on the Moon. Choosing the right landing site is an important step in planning successful lunar missions. Scientists and mission planners need to understand the Moon's surface conditions before deciding where a spacecraft should land.

However, the lunar surface is not uniform. Different areas have different elevations, slopes, sunlight conditions, shadows, and communication possibilities. These factors make choosing a safe and suitable landing location a challenging process.

Our goal is to make this process easier by using scientific data and interactive technology.

## 2. The Main Problem

Finding a suitable landing site requires analyzing several scientific factors at the same time.

Some areas have steep slopes or uneven terrain, which may make landing difficult. Other locations experience long periods of darkness, limiting sunlight availability. Communication with Earth can also be challenging depending on the selected location.

Therefore, users need a simple way to explore different lunar locations, understand their conditions, and compare them before making a decision.

Lunar Landing Site Navigator – Detailed Project Description

1. Project Overview

Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive 3D web platform designed to help users explore the Moon and evaluate potential landing locations using scientific data.

The main idea is to transform complex lunar information into an accessible visual experience. Instead of requiring users to examine separate scientific datasets, our platform brings important information together in one place.

The website combines 3D visualization, NASA scientific data, interactive maps, and landing-site evaluation to help users understand the conditions of different lunar locations.

Our platform is designed for scientists, researchers, students, space enthusiasts, and anyone interested in lunar exploration.

2. Project Concept and Design

The website starts with an immersive interface featuring a realistic 3D visualization of the Moon.

Users can explore the Moon through an interactive environment rather than simply viewing a static image. The design aims to create an engaging experience while keeping scientific information clear and easy to understand.

An astronaut guide character is also included to introduce users to the platform and help explain its main features.

The interface is designed to combine realistic space visuals with simple navigation, allowing users to move between exploration, data visualization, and landing-site evaluation.

3. Main Features

A. Interactive 3D Moon

The first main feature is an interactive 3D Moon model.

Users can:

  • View the Moon from different angles.
  • Rotate and explore its surface.
  • Zoom in to examine different regions.
  • Interact with the Moon to begin exploring potential landing locations.

This feature makes lunar exploration more visual and engaging.
